items.note: The page builds one forward invocation (gather/scatter through central wires, side wires cancelling unwanted intersection sizes, subtract and undo rows), proves y<-y+x independent of scratch, then chains three stages with the middle one inverted to get (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a), and counts the wires, in both bit and complex versions, as the paper does (lines 653-783).
A definition: "Fix the ground-set size h=100 ... Let T be the set of three-element subsets of [h], so that v=binom(h,3)=161700 counts them"; value checked correct.
Banks are indexed by a in T^3, so "N=v^3=4227952113000000 for the size of each bank" follows; m=h^3=1000000 is set as in the paper. Values checked correct.

"A stage covers all v^2 choices of the other two coordinates, each with its own invocation and scratch wires, so there are I=3v^2=78440670000 invocations" matches the paper's reasoning (lines 670-677); value correct.

Defined as in the paper (F_2 scalars, neighbours when |S cap S'|=1) and justified: the central coefficient is 1 exactly at intersection one besides S'=S, so those are the pairs side wires must cancel.
Neighbours are "the distinct triples with even intersection (zero or two)", motivated by the central coefficient table -1/2,0,1/2,1, which is nonzero and unwanted exactly at intersections 0 and 2.

The page computes the net target change (JV+RG)x, free of the initial scratch values, and checks its coefficients case by case in both constructions, concluding "one forward invocation changes y_S to y_S+x_S and leaves every other value unchanged", following the paper's proof (lines 741-759).

The schedule is described in the paper's row order: subtract injection and scatter, copy and gather, scatter and inject, "then undoes gather and copy, restoring gamma, sigma"; the eight-row table is condensed but no row is missing.
Same computation as the paper with sigma, gamma for a, c: subtract J sigma+R gamma, scratch becomes sigma+Vx, gamma+Gx, add R(gamma+Gx)+J(sigma+Vx), restore; net "(JV+RG)x, free of sigma, gamma".

Gather and scatter are given explicitly just before, so the coefficient |S cap S'| (mod 2) is read off their composition; the page states it as "|S cap S'| mod 2 is 1 for S'=S and intersection one, else 0". The composition is left implicit, as in the paper.
"Injection adds sum_{S':|S cap S'|=1} A_{SS'}, cancelling intersection one since 1+1=0", and intersections 0 and 2 are already 0 while the self coefficient is 1, matching the paper.
With C_* gathering sum x_{S'} and scatter adding (sum_{i in S} C_i - C_*)/2, the coefficient (|S cap S'|-1)/2 follows; the page also tabulates it correctly for intersections 0..3.

Injection with coefficient -(|S cap S'|-1)/2 cancels intersections zero and two via the copy; "Intersection one is already 0, and the self coefficient is (3-1)/2=1, as a triple is not its own neighbour", as in the paper.

The page runs forward, inverse (X<-X-Y), forward and writes the chain (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) at every a, with scratch restored per invocation, following the paper (lines 761-764). Its description of the inverse schedule is slightly imprecise (see errors), but the net effect X<-X-Y and restoration hold.

dropped: the counting reason: 3 choices of the shared element of S and binom(97,2) choices of the other two elements from the 97 outside S
items.note: "A triple has z_b=3 binom(97,2)=13968 neighbours" is given as a formula with a citation, with no explanation of what the factors count; the value is correct.

dropped: the counting reason for each term: binom(97,3) disjoint triples from the 97 elements outside S, and 3*97 triples sharing two elements (3 choices of the pair, 97 of the third element)
items.note: The page names the case split "(intersection zero plus two)" but only cites the count for each term; the value 147731 is correct.
Follows from the wires introduced earlier: central wires C_i, i in [h] (100), and "A further central wire C_*" in the complex construction (101).

"Ordered pairs are counted: v z_b side wires per invocation" plus c_b central wires per invocation, times I invocations, plus the two banks of N, gives W_b=2N+I(vz_b+c_b); the value 177176569091445000000 checks out. The 2N term is left implicit but follows from "N for the size of each bank".
Same assembly for the complex network, W_c=2N+I(vz_c+c_c)=1873807244643542670000 (value checks out), and "All these numbers are fixed, independent of input length".

errors.quote: The inverse schedule, the forward one with target updates negated, performs $X\gets X-Y$
errors.problem: The paper uses "the inverse forward schedule", i.e. the inverse of the forward schedule: rows in reverse order, each gate inverted. The page instead calls it the forward schedule with its target updates negated, keeping the row order. That is a different gate sequence. It also effects X<-X-Y and restores the scratch, so the argument is unchanged, but it is not literally the inverse schedule.
